newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Thakral expects 2nd half to match 1st.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Thakral expects 2nd half to match 1st.

text.p: Hotel owner and operator, Thakral Holdings Ltd (THG) said on Tuesday it expected its second half net earnings would match its first half result.

"THG is positioned for further increases in profitability with the expectation that second half net profit will be approximately equivalent to the first half," managing director, David Connors said in a statement.

Earlier Thakral posted a half year net profit of A$13.82 million, up from A$6.78 million in the same period a year earlier. It set an interim dividend of 2.5 cents per share, up from 2.0 cents a year earlier.

"The 10 hotels owned by THG have performed very strongly compared to the previous half year to December 31, with a 21.5 percent increase in the hotel division profit to A$19.3 million on a revenue increase of 13 percent to A$84.9 million," Thakral managing director David Connors said in the results statement.
"The rise in hotel operating profit was mainly due to a 7.4 percent increase in average room rate to A$127.09...together with some improvements in operating efficiences," he said.
"THG is well positioned to take advantage of continuing room rate growth," he said.
THG is 50 percent owned by interests associated with the Thakral family in Singapore.
Connors later told reporters that the room rate of the company's hotels in Melbourne had improved 15 percent over the previous corresponding period while the rate in Sydney had risen 12.5 percent.
"Melbourne is coming off a slightly lower base, certainly demand in Melbourne is quite strong -- we have been able to get strong corporate business (in Melbourne)," Connors said.

THG's 50 percent stake in Pacific Hotels Unit Trust (PCH) had increased to A$13.5 million since December 31 as a result of the purchase of the 405 room Melbourne Hilton on the Park Hotel on January 15.
THG's partner in PCH is Singapore listed Thakral Corp which is 75 percent owned by the Thakral family.
Connors said the company's All Seasons Premier Pacific Bay Resort in Coffs Harbour in New South Wales had opened on time and on budget in September.
In addition the company had sold and settled 18 of 28 apartments at the site in the first half.
"Since then we have sold more and we've started to sell the 'Diggers Estate' residential land," he said.
At 3.40 p.m (0440 GMT), Thakral shares were one cent higher at 83 cents.
